title: Understand Requirements and Identify Constraints
learningObjectives: Explain requirements and constraints in a problem statement.
Distinguish mandatory behavior from optional preferences.
Identify inputs, outputs, assumptions, and success criteria.
Create normal, boundary, and invalid test cases.
Apply requirement clarification to a small scenario.

understand.concept: Requirements describe what a solution must do; constraints limit acceptable solutions such as ranges, timing, resources, formats, permissions, or performance. Clarify goal, users, inputs, outputs, success criteria, edge cases, and assumptions before implementation.
understand.whyItMatters: Clarifying requirements prevents building something that works technically but solves the wrong problem or violates a hidden limit.
understand.analogy: Planning a journey by confirming the destination, timing, budget, and restrictions before choosing a route.
understand.analogyLimit: Requirements may change or conflict. Document assumptions and confirm uncertain details rather than treating them as facts.

explain.narrative: Turn vague requests into testable statements. Separate required behavior from optional enhancements, state assumptions, and test ordinary, boundary, and invalid cases.

guidedTask.title: Guided practice: Clarify a delivery-fee request
guidedTask.instructions: Turn the vague request 'calculate a delivery fee' into a testable mini-specification.
steps: Rewrite the request as one clear goal.
Identify at least three constraints or assumptions.
Define two normal test cases and one boundary or failure case.
Identify one question that must be clarified before coding.
guidedTask.starterCode: // Plan in plain language or pseudocode. No playground is required.

independentTask.title: Independent practice: Define a fair fee calculator
independentTask.instructions: Create a short requirement plan for a delivery-fee calculator.
requirements: State the goal and intended user.
List inputs, outputs, constraints, and assumptions.
Write three test cases including a boundary or invalid case.
Explain one ambiguous requirement that needs confirmation.
Describe how you would verify the solution.

hints: Start with the goal in plain language.
Make assumptions and expected results explicit.
Separate required behavior from optional enhancements.
Include a boundary or failure case.
Explain how your test cases demonstrate the requirements.
